blocking: The accent system uses burgundy #9E1B32 instead of the specified Anar red #D10C0C.
Repeated ruled columns contradict the explicit no-grid-hairlines direction.

fixes.what: Set --red to #D10C0C and match the existing red wordmark artwork’s fill without retyping or rebuilding it. Use brown for small text wherever the brighter red cannot provide sufficient contrast.
fixes.why: The current burgundy changes the brand’s character throughout the page.

fixes.what: Remove the repeated border-top rules from these column layouts; retain hierarchy through spacing, numbers and headings. Preserve the intentional journey line and poster frame.
fixes.why: The repeated rules make the cream sections feel like a ruled template rather than the specified brand composition.

fixes.what: Coordinate the mobile arch and wordmark positions so the wordmark overlaps the arch’s lower portion, retaining clear space for the tagline and header controls.
fixes.why: At 390px, the arch ends around y=475 while the lettering begins around y=628; the signature composition separates into two disconnected elements.

fixes.what: Give the nine-stop journey its own wider content area with smaller desktop gutters; retain the vertical arrangement until all nine labels fit without mid-word wrapping. Remove overflow-wrap:anywhere from stop headings.
fixes.why: The 1100px border-box container loses roughly 317px to gutters at 1440px, leaving about 80px per stop and undermining the intended elegant horizontal line.

fixes.where: assets/css/site.css — .form__row and .field; index.html — first inquiry row
fixes.what: Bottom-align fields within each form row and give single-line inputs a consistent height, keeping the names helper directly beneath its label.
fixes.why: The desktop email input starts higher and appears taller than the names input; this visible misalignment weakens an otherwise restrained inquiry layout.
